answer: Each identity claims one garden dune plot, locks a 70-credit bond, and keys an opal seal to a sieve set. It sifts dune sand through sieves and files weights per mesh. Auditors resieve a sample and recompute the curve from sieve table; mismatch over 4%, a reused seal, or a copied weight set burns the bond. The first plot costs 34; the kth costs 34+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6028 and 1,000 fakes cost 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-sieve ring fails because each seal binds one sieve set and one plot, and resieving exposes shared sand. Honest claimants pay 34 once and redeem after audit.
